resources.string: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, and draw your legs gently toward your chest.
Lie back and raise one leg. Hold behind the thigh and gently draw it toward you, keeping the knee softly straight.
Sit tall with the soles of your feet together. Let your knees relax outward without pushing them down.
Step the named leg back, keep that knee straight without locking it, and its heel down. Bend the front knee gently. Use a stable wall or railing if needed.
Hold a stable wall or railing. Bend the named knee and gently bring that heel toward your bottom, keeping knees close. Skip if support is unavailable or balance feels difficult.
Kneel in a split stance, gently tuck your pelvis, and keep your spine neutral as you shift forward.
Place the named heel a short step forward with toes up. Bend the other knee and hinge gently at the hips with a long back; rest hands on the bent thigh.
Step the named leg back, keep its heel down, and soften both knees. Stay upright and use a stable wall or railing if you need balance.
Stand with both feet grounded. Bring the named arm across your chest and gently support it above or below the elbow; keep the shoulder relaxed.
Stand tall, draw your shoulders gently down and back, and lift your chest slightly without arching your lower back.
Reach both arms forward with hands together. Gently round your upper back and let your shoulder blades move apart; keep your knees soft.
Raise one arm and bend the elbow so your hand rests behind your head. Rest the other hand above that elbow and apply only gentle pressure; keep your ribs relaxed.
Place both hands on a fixed, sturdy surface around waist height. Step back and hinge at your hips, keeping your back long. Skip if suitable support is unavailable.
Stand beside a wall. Reach both hands toward it and gently lean your hips away until you feel a mild stretch along your side. Keep both feet grounded.
Place one forearm against a wall with the elbow at shoulder height. Turn your chest gently away until you feel a mild stretch. Keep the shoulder relaxed; do not force the turn.
Hold a fixed support. Swing one leg gently forward and back with a soft knee, keeping your torso tall.
Hold a fixed rail. Swing one leg gently across and out to the side while keeping your pelvis level.
Lift one bent knee, open the thigh gently to the side, then lower it. Alternate legs without twisting the planted knee. Use support if needed.
With soft knees, rise gently onto the balls of both feet. Lower your heels, then lift your toes slightly. Rock slowly without losing balance.
Stand with soft knees. Shift weight a little across the soles from side to side, keeping feet nearly flat. Keep the range small; do not roll onto your ankles.
Bring feet close and soften your knees. Rest hands lightly above the knees and make tiny comfortable circles. Keep feet planted and never force rotation.
Stand tall with soft knees. Reach one arm overhead and bend gently sideways. Return upright and alternate, keeping your chest facing forward.
Set one foot forward and the other back. Bend both knees to lower straight down, then rise. Keep the front knee tracking its toes and use a comfortable depth.
Stand wide. Sit your hips back over one bent knee while the other leg stays long. Return to the middle and alternate, with knees tracking toes.
Step into a runner’s lunge and place the opposite hand beside the front foot. Gently open your chest toward the front knee and reach up. Return and alternate sides without forcing the twist.
Stand wide with soft knees. Hinge at the hips and reach toward the opposite shin or foot as the other arm opens upward. Return through the middle and alternate. Touching the toes is optional.
Stand tall. Lift one knee and turn your chest gently toward it. Lower the foot, face forward and alternate. Do not pull or press on the knee.
Stand tall and briefly hold one ankle behind you, with the knee pointing down beside the other knee. Release, step and alternate. Use a fixed support if needed; do not arch your back.
Step one heel forward with toes raised. Soften the supporting knee, hinge from your hips and sweep your hands down beside the front leg. Rise smoothly and alternate.
March or jog lightly in place, alternating knees at a comfortable height and swinging opposite arms. Stay upright and land softly. A low march is fine.
March or jog lightly in place, alternating heels toward your buttocks. Keep thighs near vertical, torso tall and land softly. Do not force heel contact.
Stand wide and bend one knee while keeping the other leg long. Sit your hips back, keep feet planted and hold gentle tension along the inner thigh.
Sit with legs comfortably apart and knees soft. Hinge gently forward from your hips with a long back, resting hands on the floor in front. Do not force your chest down.
Stand wide with soft knees. Rest one hand on the thigh, reach the other arm overhead and bend gently sideways. Keep your chest facing forward.
Cross one foot in front with both feet grounded and knees soft. Hinge gently from your hips toward your shins. Rise slowly and uncross before changing sides. Use support for balance if needed.
From hands and knees, tuck your toes and lift hips up and back. Keep knees softly bent to lengthen your back. Heels may stay lifted. Lower your knees to finish.

Bring one knee forward with the heel toward the opposite groin, and extend the other leg behind. Support the front-side hip with a cushion. Keep hips facing forward without forcing the shin square. Stop for knee discomfort; use lying figure four instead.

Sit with one leg extended and its knee soft. Bend the other knee out with its sole against the inner thigh. Hinge gently toward the long leg. Keep the bent foot in front of your pelvis, never tucked behind.
Place one heel forward with toes raised and soften the supporting knee. Hinge gently from your hips and, if comfortable, lightly draw the front forefoot toward your shin. Do not force the reach.

Sit tall with one leg long and the opposite foot flat outside its thigh. Place one hand behind you and turn your chest gently toward the bent knee. Rest the other hand lightly on the thigh; do not lever against the knee.
Add at least one posture to continue.
